newsitem.title: CROATIA: Pliva, Zagrebacka hit new records.
newsitem.headline: Pliva, Zagrebacka hit new records.

text.p: Croatian blue chips Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka hit historic highs on Wednesday in another record-breaking session on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, traders said.
Heavily traded drugs firm Pliva added seven kuna to 570 with some 4,000 shares changing hands an hour before the 1400 (1200 GMT) close.
Its 1/5 GDRs fetched $17.825 on the London Stock Exchange, compared to $17.525 on Tuesday, though receeding from $17.85 at the open.
Zagrebacka's ordinaries also firmed seven kuna to 2,447 following a rise of its 1/10 GDRs to $37.75 from $37.25 each on London's Seaq.
"The London increase and firming dollar are really helping though prices in Zagreb may be overshooting those in London," said Denis Fuduric of IB Austria.
The bank sold only 50 ordinary shares this morning compared to a volume of several thousand each day over the past week or so, which some traders said might be a sign of saturation.
But Fuduric foresaw no end to blue chip gains and said rumours about their buoyant first half results were bound to boost trade and further prop up prices.
Another fully-listed bank stock -- Varazdinska Banka first series -- also firmed to touch 216-218 kuna, recovering from a recent slump.
Demand for repair docks Viktor Lenac seemed to have slackened after it rose too much too quickly after the listing earlier this month. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
